Libolo|Recreativo do Libolo]] (17) | longest winless = {{Nowrap|[[Estrela Clube Primeiro de Maio|1º de Maio]]; [[União Sport Clube do Uíge|União Uíge]] (14)}} | longest losses = [[União Sport Clube do Uíge|União do Uíge]] (8) | matches = 240 | total goals = 509 | prevseason = [[2013 Girabola|2013]] | nextseason = [[2015 Girabola|2015]] }} The '''2014 [[Girabola]]''' was the 36th season of top-tier football league in [[Angola]]. The season ran from 21 February to 8 November 2014. [[Kabuscorp S.C.P.|Kabuscorp]] were the defending champions, having won their first Angolan championship in 2013. The league comprised 16 teams, the bottom three of which were relegated to the 2015 [[Segundona]].{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ango2011.html |title=Angola 2011 |date=6 May 2011 |access-date=20 May 2011 |author=King, Ian}} ==Teams== A total of 16 teams contested the league, including 13 sides from the [[2013 Girabola|2013 season]] and three promoted from the 2013 [[Segundona]], [[S.L. Benfica (Lubango)|Benfica do Lubango]], [[Sporting Clube de Cabinda|Sporting de Cabinda]], [[União Sport Clube do Uíge|União SC do Uíge]]. On the other hand, [[Porcelana Futebol Clube do Cazengo|Porcelana FC]], [[Atlético Petróleos do Namibe|Atlético do Namibe]], [[Santos Futebol Clube de Angola|Santos FC]] were the last three teams of the [[2013 Girabola|2013 season]] and played in the [[Segundona]] for the 2014 season.
